title: Evaluation sentinel: automatic regression alerts for config/model deltas using canary corpora
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
As we push model weight changes, tokenizer tweaks, runtime config updates (batching, KV cache behavior, quantization profiles) and routing rules, teams need deterministic, automated signals when user-facing quality changes. Current eval runs are ad-hoc: PR authors manually trigger evals against large golden snapshots or depend on weekly jobs. This causes noise and slow detection of regressions tied to configuration deltas.

Goal:
Implement an "evaluation sentinel" subsystem: a lightweight subscription model that 1) lets a repo, config, or deployment subscribe canonical canary corpora (stewarded prompt bundles) and evaluation metrics, 2) automatically runs a fast statistical regression test when an associated model/config change is proposed or rolled out, and 3) emits actionable alerts with suggested rollback/fallback steps if thresholds are breached.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: per-config/model change hooks (CI/webhook), a canary-corpus registry reference, fast eval runner with configurable sampling, significance testing (bootstrap/paired tests), alerting to Slack/console and PR comments, and a simple RBAC check for which prompt bundles can be used for automated triggers.
- Out of scope for this ticket: full golden snapshot archival migration, long-running exhaustive suite runs, and UI for corpus curation (will integrate with Console in follow-up).

Design overview (high level):
1) Subscription model: configs/models have metadata field eval_subscriptions which lists canary corpus ids, metric definitions (e.g., exact-match-ratio, semantic-similarity delta), and severity thresholds. Subscriptions are declarative and stored in the ConfigService.
2) Trigger points: CI on PR for model/config change, deployment canary rollouts, and API-based mutation endpoints. The trigger sends a webhook to the sentinel service with diff metadata and a reference to the active model/config revision.
3) Fast eval runner: runs N-shot sampling from the stewarded canary corpus (configurable N; default 200) with lightweight scoring pipelines (fast-embed similarity + token-level checks). Uses cached KV prefixes where applicable to reduce runtime cost.
4) Statistical layer: run paired bootstrap and compute 95% CI on metric deltas; require both magnitude threshold and p-value threshold for an actionable regression.
5) Alerting and remediation: if regression detected, create PR comment summarizing delta, post to #runtime-regressions Slack channel, and mark the change as blocked in DeploymentService. Optionally enqueue automatic rollback when severity = high.
6) Governance: only steward accounts with ACL for a corpus may opt that corpus into an automated subscription; all runs produce an immutable result artifact with signature and trace to the corpus version and trigger id.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Declarative eval_subscriptions field implemented in ConfigService schema and visible via config API (read/write guard: admins only).
- [ ] Sentinel accepts webhook triggers from CI and returns run status synchronously for PR checks (timeout 10m) and async for rollouts.
- [ ] Fast eval runner can run default N=200 samples in <6 minutes on a small Dedicated instance using cached prefixes.
- [ ] Statistical test infra computes paired bootstrap CIs and produces clear pass/fail + delta summary.
- [ ] Alerts posted to Slack and PR comments contain corpus id, sample size, metric baseline, delta, CI, and suggested action (block/monitor/rollback).
- [ ] Immutable result artifact (signed) saved to EvalStore with links in alert and PR comment.

Trade-offs and decisions to record now:
- Sampling vs exhaustive: we prioritize fast detection for canary corpora (sampling) rather than running full golden snapshots on every PR to keep CI latency acceptable.
- Metrics: begin with 2 metric families (exactness and semantic similarity) and provide a plugin hook for additional evaluators later.
- Significance testing: bootstrap paired tests are robust for small N and don't require strong distributional assumptions; we'll standardize on 95% CI and one-sided regression checks for initial rollout.
- Automation vs human gating: high-severity detections will optionally auto-rollback only when the deployment is a canary (not full production) and when the change came from an automated pipeline with approvals; otherwise the system blocks progression and notifies stewards.

Security and privacy considerations:
- Corpus access is restricted by ACLs; automated runs must run in the same VPC/private environment when corpus is private.
- Result artifacts may contain prompt text; storage is encrypted and access-audited.

Next steps / implementation tasks:
- Schema change: ConfigService eval_subscriptions field (ENG-51235).
- Sentinel service skeleton + webhook contract (ENG-51236).
- Fast eval runner integration and caching (ENG-51237).
- Statistical library and result artifact format (ENG-51238).
- CI integration PR and GitHub action (ENG-51239).
- Slack/Console alert plumbing and PR commenter (ENG-51240).

Notes: this ticket focuses on the infra and API; companion PM ticket will specify default corpus selection and stewarding process for initial customers.
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial RFC posted. Key risk: sampling variance on very small canaries — propose default N=200 and an override per-subscription.

2026-03-11 Diego Martinez: Prototype runner shows 4.7m median run time for 200 samples using existing micro-Dedicated. We'll aim for sub-6m target. Need to ensure KV cache warm-up included in measurements.
2026-03-11 Aisha Khan (Product): PM thumbs-up on developer UX; request that PR comments include a clear link to rollback runbook and a one-line summary for non-technical reviewers.
2026-03-12 Security review (Omar Patel): Corpus ACL enforcement must be server-side; cannot rely on client-supplied corpus ids. Marking security_review_required=true.
